tasks.title: Free playground
tasks.instructions: Write any Python you like and press Run. It's a scratchpad for trying out ideas from your lessons.
requirements: Experiment freely - nothing here is graded or saved
tasks.hint: Try changing a value and running the program again to see how the output changes.
tasks.starterCode: # Write any Python code here and press Run

tasks.title: Your first program
tasks.instructions: Write a program that introduces you using print().
requirements: Print the result of adding two numbers
Add a comment explaining your code
tasks.hint: Each print() puts its text on a new line. Numbers don't need quotes: print(7 + 5).
tasks.starterCode:
# Your first program
# Use print() to show three lines

tasks.title: Shopping bill
tasks.instructions: Store the number of pens and notebooks you bought in variables, then work out and print the total number of items.
requirements: Create a variable for pens and one for notebooks
Create a variable total that adds them

tasks.title: Type detective
tasks.instructions: A friend's age was saved as text: age_text = "14". Print its type, convert it to a whole number, then print the age they will be in 5 years.
requirements: Convert it with int() into a new variable
tasks.hint: "14" + 5 is an error, but int("14") + 5 works.

tasks.title: Greeting program
tasks.instructions: Write a Python program that asks the user for their name and prints a greeting.
requirements: Ask for the user's name with input()
Print a greeting that includes the name
tasks.example:
Enter your name: Arnav
Hello Arnav
tasks.hint: name = input("Enter your name: ") stores whatever the user types.

tasks.title: Birthday maths
tasks.instructions: Ask the user for their name and age, then tell them how old they will be next year using an f-string.
requirements: Read the age and convert it with int()
Print a sentence with an f-string
tasks.example:
Name: Meera
Age: 15
Meera, next year you will be 16
tasks.hint: input() always gives text - wrap it in int() before adding 1.

tasks.title: Number comparer
tasks.instructions: Ask the user for two whole numbers and print the result of comparing them.
requirements: Print whether the first is greater than the second
tasks.example:
First: 8
Second: 3
8 > 3 is True
8 == 3 is False
tasks.hint: print(a > b) prints True or False.

tasks.title: Can I vote?
tasks.instructions: Ask for the user's age. If they are 18 or older print that they can vote, otherwise print how many years they have to wait.
requirements: Convert the age to a number
Calculate the years left in the else branch
tasks.example:
Age: 15
You can vote in 3 years
tasks.hint: Indent the lines that belong to if and else by 4 spaces (use the Tab key above the keyboard).

tasks.title: Grade calculator
tasks.instructions: Ask for a mark out of 100 and print a grade: A for 90 and above, B for 75 and above, C for 50 and above, otherwise "Keep practising".
requirements: Read the mark as a number
tasks.hint: Python checks each condition from top to bottom and runs the first one that is True.

tasks.title: Times table
tasks.instructions: Ask for a number and print its times table from 1 to 10 using a for loop.

tasks.title: Countdown
tasks.instructions: Ask for a starting number and count down to 1 with a while loop, then print "Lift off!".
requirements: Print Lift off! at the end

tasks.title: Marks analyser
tasks.instructions: Store five marks in a list, add one more with append(), then print the highest, the lowest and the average mark.
requirements: Print max, min and the average
